Current Road LTL content maturity must be assessed separately from architecture sufficiency.
Canonical Work Decomposition and WorkDefinition machine-readable contracts remain implementation-pending.
No first-class aggregate implementation-scope readiness assessment with blocker dependency closure was found.
No generic version-closed enterprise implementation-handoff manifest was found; this may be a projection/materialization issue rather than a new semantic layer.

Executor-neutral decomposition versus intended-executor stopping criteria requires boundary clarification.
Atlas can credibly support ERP/TMS operational fit-gap readiness, not full ERP-program implementation readiness.
No broad monolithic Execution Requirements layer is justified by AR0.1 evidence.
